newsitem.title: SOUTH KOREA: Seoul stocks end nearly flat, small-caps suffer.
newsitem.headline: Seoul stocks end nearly flat, small-caps suffer.

text.p: South Korean stocks closed nearly flat in Saturday's half-day session, pressured by brisk selling in smaller-capitalised stocks, brokers said.
The composite index closed at 831.18, up 0.93 points, after trading in a 821.72-831.97 range.
"The market was weak for most of the session, but gains of medium- to large-cap stocks kept the index in the positive territory towards the close," said Hyundai Securities broker Koh Kyung-bae.
Declining stocks beat advancers by 472 to 382 while 152 closed unchanged.

Market speculation that state prosecutors would start investigating suspected price manipulation on stocks which had risen recently caused heavy selling of small-cap shares, brokers said. The speculation could not be immediately confirmed.
"Instead, bargain hunting set in for stocks believed to be safe from the investigations," said Koh.
Samsung Electronics, the bluest of South Korean blue chips, gained 500 won to close at 67,500. Tai Lim Packaging, which has fallen sharply in recent weeks, closed up 1,600 won to 28,900.
Investors appeared to shrug off an investigation orderd by President Kim Young-sam into bribery charges made against former defence minister Lee Yang-ho, brokers said.
Opposition lawmakers accused Lee of having taken bribes in return for leaking classified military information on a combat helicopter project to an arms dealer in 1995.
